## 1. Purpose

This SOP establishes a single, program-wide standard for labeling field
samples, completing chain of custody (COC) documentation, and
transporting samples from the field to the laboratory. Consistent
labeling prevents sample mix-ups, and a complete chain of custody
ensures that data are legally defensible and scientifically traceable.
These procedures apply to all sample types (water, soil, sediment,
biological tissue, air filters) collected by the EA Program.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** All environmental samples collected during EA Program
  field activities, whether analyzed in-house or submitted to an
  external laboratory
- **Does not apply to:** Internal laboratory standards and reagents
  (labeled per [SOP-L005](../lab_sops/SOP-L005-chemical-inventory.qmd));
  data files and digital records (see
  [SOP-L801](../lab_sops/SOP-L801-rstudio-github.qmd))
- **Location:** All EA Program field sites, vehicles, and laboratory
  receiving areas (SGM 133, 134)


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Project Lead | Approve sample ID scheme for each project; designate
                      receiving personnel                                  |
| Field Lead        | Verify labels and COC forms before leaving the field    |
| Trained Personnel | Label samples and complete COC per this SOP             |
| Receiving Personnel | Accept custody, verify sample condition, log receipt  |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent sampling           |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Some sample containers include chemical preservatives
  (sulfuric acid, nitric acid, sodium thiosulfate). Handle
  pre-preserved bottles with care. Refer to
  [SOP-L003](../lab_sops/SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).
- **Physical:** Coolers loaded with ice and sample bottles can be
  heavy. Use proper lifting technique.
- **Biological:** Soil and water samples may contain pathogens. Wear
  nitrile gloves when handling samples.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses (when handling preserved bottles)

### Emergency Procedures

For acid preservative spills, neutralize with baking soda and flush
with water. Refer to
[SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) and
[SOP-L004 Chemical Spill Response](../lab_sops/SOP-L004-chemical-spill-response.qmd).


## 5. Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Waterproof labels (adhesive)          | Pre-printed or blank; must survive moisture and ice |
| Permanent marker (Sharpie, fine tip)  | For writing on bottles and bags          |
| Clear packing tape                    | For protecting labels from water damage  |
| Chain of custody forms (printed)      | Blank forms stored in SGM 133            |
| Custody seals (tamper-evident tape)   | For sealing coolers before transport     |
| Coolers with ice or ice packs         | Maintain samples at approximately 4 C   |
| Ziplock bags                          | For double-bagging soil samples and protecting labels |
| Field notebook                        | For cross-referencing sample IDs         |
| Sample log sheet                      | Printed template (Appendix A)            |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Sample Identification Scheme

All EA Program samples use the following ID format:

`PROJECT-SITE-MATRIX-YYYYMMDD-NN`

where:

| Field     | Description                            | Example         |
|:----------|:---------------------------------------|:----------------|
| PROJECT   | Two- to four-letter project code       | WLD (Wildlands) |
| SITE      | Three-letter site abbreviation         | BFS (Bernard Field Station) |
| MATRIX    | Two-letter matrix code (see below)     | SW (surface water) |
| YYYYMMDD  | Collection date                        | 20260519        |
| NN        | Sequential sample number for the day   | 01, 02, ...     |

**Matrix codes:**

| Code | Matrix                    |
|:-----|:--------------------------|
| SW   | Surface water             |
| GW   | Groundwater               |
| ST   | Stormwater                |
| SL   | Soil                      |
| SD   | Sediment                  |
| PT   | Plant tissue              |
| BM   | Biological / macroinvertebrate |
| AF   | Air filter                |
| FB   | Field blank               |
| FD   | Field duplicate           |
| EB   | Equipment blank           |

Projects may extend this scheme with additional fields (e.g., depth,
treatment). Document any project-specific additions in the project
README file and field notebook.

### 6.2 Labeling Samples

1. **Before going to the field**, pre-label as many containers as
   possible. Use waterproof labels or write directly on the container
   with permanent marker. Cover all handwritten labels with clear
   packing tape to prevent smearing.
2. At a minimum, every sample container must display:
   - Sample ID (per Section 6.1)
   - Date and time of collection
   - Collector's initials
   - Preservative (if any), e.g., "H~2~SO~4~" or "None"
3. For soil samples in bags, write the sample ID on both the bag and
   an internal tag (a slip of paper inside the bag) in case the
   external label becomes illegible.
4. For pre-preserved bottles provided by an analytical lab, do not
   remove the lab's label. Add the EA sample ID on a separate label
   or directly on the bottle.
5. Record every sample ID, time, location, and any field observations
   in the field notebook and on the sample log sheet (Appendix A).

### 6.3 Quality Control Samples

Include the following QC samples in every sampling event. Label them
using the matrix codes FB, FD, and EB so they are clearly
distinguishable from field samples.

| QC Type          | Frequency                  | Procedure                        |
|:-----------------|:---------------------------|:---------------------------------|
| Field blank (FB) | 1 per sampling event       | Fill a sample bottle with DI water at the site; preserve and handle identically to field samples |
| Field duplicate (FD) | 1 per 10 samples (minimum 1 per event) | Collect a second sample at the same location immediately after the primary sample |
| Equipment blank (EB) | 1 per sampling event    | Rinse decontaminated sampling equipment with DI water; collect the rinse water |

### 6.4 Chain of Custody

A COC form must accompany every set of samples submitted for analysis,
whether to the EA Program lab or to an external laboratory. The COC
establishes an unbroken record of sample possession from collection to
final analysis.

**Completing the COC form:**

1. Fill in the header: project name, PI name, date, and contact
   information.
2. List each sample by its sample ID (Section 6.1), collection date
   and time, number and type of containers, preservative used, and
   analyses requested.
3. Note the total number of containers being transferred.
4. Record any relevant field conditions (e.g., "high turbidity,"
   "post-storm event").
5. The person relinquishing the samples signs and dates the
   "Relinquished by" field.
6. The person receiving the samples signs and dates the "Received by"
   field, inspects the samples for damage or discrepancies, and notes
   any issues.
7. If custody transfers occur in multiple steps (e.g., field to
   vehicle, vehicle to lab), each transfer requires a signature pair.
8. Record the COC form number in the field notebook for
   cross-reference (see
   [SOP-F003](SOP-F003-field-notebook-protocols.qmd), Section 9).

### 6.5 Sample Transport

1. Place all sample containers upright in a cooler with ice or frozen
   ice packs. Target a temperature of approximately 4 C for water and
   soil samples unless the analytical method specifies otherwise.
2. Use ziplock bags or bubble wrap to prevent bottles from breaking
   during transport.
3. Seal the cooler with tamper-evident custody seals across the lid
   opening. Write the date and your initials on each seal.
4. Transport samples to the laboratory as quickly as possible. Most
   water quality parameters have maximum hold times (see table below).
   Do not leave samples in a vehicle overnight unless the vehicle is
   temperature-controlled.

**Common maximum hold times:**

| Parameter                  | Preservative       | Max Hold Time |
|:---------------------------|:-------------------|:--------------|
| Bacteria (total coliform, *E. coli*) | Na~2~S~2~O~3~ (in bottle) | 6 hours |
| Nutrients (N, P)           | H~2~SO~4~ to pH < 2 | 28 days      |
| Metals (dissolved)         | HNO~3~ to pH < 2   | 180 days     |
| pH, conductivity, turbidity | None (measure in field or ASAP) | 15 minutes (field); analyze same day (lab) |
| Soil moisture              | None               | Analyze within 24 hours |
| Soil for nutrient analysis | Cool to 4 C        | 28 days      |

::: {.callout-important}
Samples for bacteria analysis (Colilert) must be processed within
6 hours of collection. Plan field logistics accordingly. See
[SOP-L305](../lab_sops/SOP-L305-colilert-quanti-tray.qmd).
:::

### 6.6 Receiving Samples in the Laboratory

1. Upon arrival at the lab, the receiving person opens the cooler,
   checks the custody seal for tampering, and signs the COC form.
2. Verify that the number of containers matches the COC listing.
   Note any discrepancies on the COC form.
3. Check sample temperature using a thermometer placed among the
   bottles. Record the temperature on the COC form.
4. Transfer samples to the appropriate storage location:
   - Water samples: refrigerator at 4 C
     ([SOP-L106](../lab_sops/SOP-L106-refrigerators-freezers.qmd))
   - Soil samples: refrigerator at 4 C (for short-term) or freezer
     (for archiving)
   - Biological samples: freezer at -20 C or -80 C as required
5. File the signed COC form with the project records.


## 7. Quality Control

- The field lead reviews all labels and the COC form before leaving
  the field site.
- Receiving personnel verify sample count, condition, and temperature
  upon arrival.
- Any broken, leaking, or incorrectly labeled samples are flagged on
  the COC form and reported to the PI within 24 hours.
- COC forms are retained for the duration of the project plus a
  minimum of 5 years.


## 8. References

- US EPA. (2002). *Guidance for Quality Assurance Project Plans* (EPA
  QA/G-5). EPA/240/R-02/009.
- APHA, AWWA, WEF. (2012). *Standard Methods for Examination of Water
  and Wastewater*. 22nd ed. Table 1060:I (sample containers,
  preservatives, and holding times).
- California SWAMP. (2017). *Quality Assurance Program Plan*.

## 10. Training Record

Before labeling and handling samples independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and
   [SOP-F003 Field Notebook Protocols](SOP-F003-field-notebook-protocols.qmd)
   in full
2. Demonstrate correct sample labeling using the project ID scheme
3. Complete a COC form correctly during a supervised field outing
4. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
